co_co_hwy_7_tributaries.blurb: These crags are scattered along Highway 7, the Peak to Peak route running south from Estes Park toward Allenspark, mostly at roughly 8,000 to 11,000 feet. The rock is granitic, with some gneiss and schist, and lines can stretch to several hundred feet. Sport slightly outnumbers trad, with a few top-ropes and boulders. Most routes fall from 5.8 to 5.11, with a decent group at 5.12 and a handful beyond. Few cliffs sit beside the road, so expect some walking and, for a number of the high ones, a long hike. The Crags, Prospect Mountain and the Ironclads are the largest sectors, and Lily Mountain offers short, mostly bolted moderates after a short flat hike.

me_acadia_national_park.blurb: Acadia sits on the Maine coast, and its climbing is on solid, coarse pink granite. Trad leads the count, followed by bouldering, then a good number of top-ropes and a few sport routes. Climbs are mostly 5.6 to 5.11 with a peak around 5.10, plus some harder lines, while most boulder problems sit between V0 and V4. Routes top out at about three pitches. Otter Cliffs and Great Head are sea cliffs, where tides, surf and weather change conditions; the Precipice has long corners and thin cracks, and MDI Bouldering gathers a large share of the boulder problems. The warm months, roughly May to late September, suit the coast best.

nc_moore_s_wall.blurb: Moore's Wall rises in Hanging Rock State Park in the North Carolina Piedmont, a short drive from Winston-Salem. The rock is juggy, steep quartzite. Bouldering accounts for the biggest share of the climbs, with trad close behind and only a small number of sport routes. Problems run from easy to hard in the V10 range, but most land between V0 and V6. Roped climbs cover a wide range, from 5.6 to 5.13 and a little beyond, concentrated at 5.10 to 5.12; the trad lines are adventurous and need confident gear placements. The area is split between the routes on the wall and several boulder zones.

ca_santa_barbara_bouldering.blurb: Santa Barbara's boulders are spread through the foothills of the Santa Ynez Mountains, on sandstone, and the climbing here is almost entirely bouldering. Problems stretch from the easiest grades into V10 and V11, with the heaviest concentration between V0 and V6. The Lizard's Mouth is the largest area and has a small cave with a traverse favored by strong climbers, while the Brickyard is known for overhanging, gymnastic problems. Skofield Park is a small city-park spot near the Rattlesnake Canyon trailhead. Painted Cave and the Creamery add smaller collections.

ut_zion_national_park.blurb: Zion is a deep, steep-walled canyon landscape in southwest Utah, with sandstone cliffs about 2,000 feet tall. The rock is soft desert sandstone that weakens when wet and can need two days or more to dry. Trad and big-wall style climbing dominates, with a fair amount of aid, some boulders, and few sport routes; bolted lines tend to be sparsely protected. Most routes sit between 5.9 and 5.11, with a smaller group at 5.12 and a few ice lines. March through May and September to early November are the most comfortable seasons, while summer can top 100 degrees even in shade. Kolob Canyon, the Mount Carmel Tunnel area and Zion Bouldering are among the larger sub-areas.
